title: Imaging the vacuum fluctuations of a quantum field
summary: Heisenberg uncertainties lead to inevitable fluctuations in the measurement outcomes for quantum-mechanical observables. For quantum fields, these uncertainties result in random spatial structures in snapshots of a field, even when the field is in its ground (vacuum) state. Such `vacuum fluctuations' are at the heart of a wide range of phenomena, from spontaneous decay processes to the Casimir force and Hawking radiation.
